whyThisShow: This is the Grateful Dead's soundboard set from Summer Jam at Watkins Glen, July 1973 — an outdoor festival that drew an estimated 600,000 people, making it one of the largest gatherings in American history at the time [source: 'one of the largest cities in the country at the time']. The Dead shared the bill with the Allman Brothers Band and The Band, and by multiple firsthand accounts the Dead played for close to two hours during the soundcheck-turned-performance on Friday [source: 'Dead logged at least two hours']. One reviewer who was there called it "one of the best concerts ever" [source: 'headed north from philly to one of the best concerts ever']. The set remains officially unreleased, which the community treats as its own kind of signal about what's sitting in the vault.
listenFor: The China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider and the Playing in the Band are the sequences most cited by listeners as the heart of the set [source: 'the China>Rider, Playin\', and Eyes']. Eyes of the World also draws specific attention [source: 'plenty more to the show - namely the China>Rider, Playin\', and Eyes']. The encore featured a cross-band Mountain Jam with the Allmans; one reviewer strongly disagreed with Butch Trucks's own assessment that it was a disaster, calling it "DOPE" and recommending it specifically to fans of both bands [source: 'it is nonetheless DOPE']. The source is a soundboard recording, so the mix is direct rather than a crowd capture.
context: July 1973 sits squarely in the Wall of Sound era, when the Dead were building toward the massive PA system that would debut in 1974. The Archive identifier (gd73-07-28.sbd.weiner.14196.sbeok.shnf) confirms a soundboard lineage. The show has never received an official release, which is notable given its historical scale. One attendee flagged that a commercially released album claiming to document Watkins Glen does not actually capture what happened that day [source: 'that album they CALL live at Watkins Glen. Sorry guys.. that was NOT recorded at WG'].
funFact: One reviewer who hitched to the show recalled that their last ride — about 35 miles out — came from a girl who lived just a few blocks from them back in Oxford, Ohio [source: 'our last ride was about 35 miles from WG, from a girl who actually lived a few blocks from us in Oxford who was going there as well'].
headline: Watkins Glen, summer '73, half a million people and a soundboard.
